1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon — adjust upward by 2–5% for early periods.  
2. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overreact and overshoot — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 7-day average.  
4. Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag — true values often exceed model by 2–8% in the 15–25 day window — apply a 1–2% upward bias for mid-horizon.  
5. Model fails to capture late-period volatility — true values often spike again after 25–30 days — add 1–3% upward adjustment for final 5–7 days.
